content: PHYLIP (Phylogeny Inference Package) is a freely available computational software suite designed for constructing evolutionary trees, also known as phylogenies. The name PHYLIP is an acronym derived from Phylogeny Inference Package. The software's source code is written in the C programming language, and precompiled executables are available for various operating systems, including Windows (95/98/NT/2000/ME/XP), MacOS 8 and 9, MacOS X, and Linux. Comprehensive documentation is provided for all programs included in the package, and this documentation is distributed as part of the software. The package was developed by Joseph Felsenstein, a professor in the Department of Genome Sciences and the Department of Biology at the University of Washington, Seattle. The PHYLIP package implements several methods for phylogenetic analysis, including parsimony, distance matrix methods, and likelihood-based approaches. It also supports advanced techniques such as bootstrapping and the generation of consensus trees. The software can handle a variety of data types, including molecular sequences, gene frequencies, restriction sites and fragments, distance matrices, and discrete characters. Each program within the package operates through a menu-driven interface, which prompts users to select options and initiate computations. Input data is read from a text file that users can prepare using any word processor or text editor. However, it is crucial that the text file is saved in a plain ASCII or Text Only format, rather than in a proprietary format specific to the word processor. Some sequence analysis programs, such as ClustalW, can generate data files in the PHYLIP format. Most programs in the PHYLIP suite look for input data in a file named infile. If this file is not found, the program prompts the user to specify the name of the data file. Output files are generated with names such as outfile and outtree. The phylogenetic trees written to the outtree file are formatted in the Newick format, which is an informal standard established in 1986 by the authors of several major phylogeny software packages. The PHYLIP package and its methods are described in detail in the book Inferring Phylogenies by Joseph Felsenstein, published in August 2003 by Sinauer Associates (ISBN 0-87893-177-5). Additional documentation and resources for the PHYLIP package are available online.
